response.sql:
WITH long_films AS (
  SELECT rating, rental_rate, rental_duration
  FROM film
  WHERE rental_duration >= 5
),
per_rating AS (
  SELECT rating,
         AVG(rental_rate / NULLIF(rental_duration, 0)) AS avg_rate_per_day,
         COUNT(*) AS films
  FROM long_films
  GROUP BY rating
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS bench
  FROM per_rating
)
SELECT p.rating,
       p.avg_rate_per_day,
       p.films,
       p.avg_rate_per_day / b.bench AS ratio_to_benchmark
FROM per_rating p
CROSS JOIN benchmark b
WHERE b.bench IS NOT NULL

assumptions.assumption: "Treating 5 days as the cutoff" is read as inclusive: a film is long-rental when rental_duration >= 5 (so 5, 6 and 7 days). The request does not say whether 5 itself counts.

Per-film value is rental_rate / rental_duration, averaged within each rating over the long-rental films. Rows with a zero duration would yield NULL and be ignored; none exist because the data runs from 3 to 7 days.
The benchmark is the unweighted AVG of the per-rating averages over the long-rental subset. Its ratio column is NULL if the benchmark is NULL, and the WHERE clause then returns no rows.

alternatives.interpretation: "Long" means strictly longer than 5 days, so only rental_duration of 6 or 7 counts.
